layers.name: Minerals, metals and gases
layers.description: Mined and refined commodities that every tool, fab and transformer depends on.
layers.expansion_note: Greenfield helium, gallium and GOES capacity takes 5-10 years; 2026 supply is fixed and rationed by price and policy.

risks.text: Qatar helium exports disrupted in 2026: roughly a third of global supply offline, spot prices doubled, no quick substitute
China produces 98% of primary refined gallium and 69% of mined rare earths, and is the leading germanium refiner, all under export controls
Grain-oriented electrical steel is a five-company oligopoly; main power transformer lead times stretched to 48-60 months
Indium phosphide supply-demand gap now exceeds DRAM and NAND, gating EML lasers for 800G/1.6T optics

watch: Qatar Ras Laffan helium restart date

layers.name: Engineered materials
layers.description: Purified and engineered inputs for lithography optics, fabs and packaging.
layers.expansion_note: Only GlobalWafers has a large-scale wafer expansion; Ajinomoto's ABF film capacity grows ~50% by 2030-32; resist plants near TSMC and Samsung come online 2026-27.

risks.text: Ajinomoto holds >95% of ABF build-up film from two Japanese plants and raised prices ~30%
Nittobo T-glass cloth effectively sole-sourced; 10-20% shortage in 2026 widening to 20% in 2027
EUV resist is three Japanese firms with 18-month qualification cycles; 2026 naphtha disruptions tightened solvent and precursor supply
Expiring low-price wafer LTAs are rolling to higher prices; spot rising ahead of contract

layers.name: Lithography subsystems and optics
layers.description: Mirrors, drive lasers, EUV sources, mechatronics and mask inspection that ASML integrates.
layers.expansion_note: Optics output is the gating item; Zeiss, Trumpf and VDL are private and scale by hiring and floor space in Oberkochen, Ditzingen and Eindhoven.

risks.text: Carl Zeiss SMT is the single source for EUV projection optics; High-NA output has not accelerated since 2024 and gates the whole ramp
TRUMPF drive lasers and VDL frames are private-company capacities that must keep pace with ASML's 2027-28 volumes
EUV source power is becoming a throughput bottleneck, pushing fabs toward higher-sensitivity resists

watch: Zeiss 0.55 NA optics shipped in H2 2026 (eight or more = on track)

layers.name: Semiconductor capital equipment
layers.description: Lithography, deposition, etch, process control, bonding and test tools.
layers.expansion_note: Capacity grows faster than spend, but a new EUV tool still arrives about two years after order; field upgrades fill the gap.

risks.text: ASML is 100% of EUV lithography; a two-year waitlist means 2028 fab plans are already tool-constrained
Export controls and China exposure shape the order book; outlook depends on customer capex and the cycle
TSMC deferred High-NA to A14 (2028), pushing the €400m-per-system revenue step out by two years

layers.name: Wafer fabrication
layers.description: Leading-edge logic foundries and IDMs turning wafers into dies.
layers.expansion_note: Capex $60-64bn in 2026; leading-edge capacity grows about half as fast as demand, so allocation and pricing do the balancing.

risks.text: Leading-edge AI logic is effectively single-sourced from TSMC in Taiwan; geopolitics, export controls and overseas-fab margin dilution are disclosed risks
AI accelerators, CPUs and networking take ~60% of N3 in 2026 and 86% in 2027; other customers get squeezed
Management says packaging capacity, not wafers, limits customers' growth
Helium cost compresses fab margins by an estimated 300-500 bp in 2026

watch: TSMC Q3 2026 call: N2 ramp, Arizona, capex

layers.name: Memory (HBM, DRAM, NAND)
layers.description: High-bandwidth memory, commodity DRAM and NAND for accelerators and servers.
layers.expansion_note: New DRAM supply takes years (Micron Idaho first wafer mid-2027); HBM eats 3-4x the wafers per bit, so bit growth lags demand until 2028.

risks.text: HBM4 allocation is decided by NVIDIA qualification; SK hynix delays, Samsung recovery and Micron gaps can reshuffle share within a quarter
HBM consumes 3-4x the wafer capacity per bit of commodity DRAM; HBM supply constrained through end-2027
Memory prices have historically fallen more than 60% when supply arrives; margins near 86% are cyclical peaks
CXMT ramps HBM from ~1% to ~12% share by 2028 and floods commodity DRAM

watch: Micron fiscal Q4 print (late Sep 2026) and HBM4 share

layers.name: Advanced packaging and substrates
layers.description: CoWoS-class packaging, OSATs and ABF substrates that turn dies into accelerators.
layers.expansion_note: The one layer where capacity is now growing faster than demand; substrates (ABF, T-glass) lag and become the next constraint.

risks.text: TSMC CoWoS is the sole packaging path for NVIDIA, AMD and Broadcom accelerators; NVIDIA takes ~60% of capacity
ABF substrate utilization >95%, lead times 26 weeks, orders secured to 2029-30; packaging cost +18-25%
Glass-core substrates (Intel, Samsung, Absolics) could strand organic-substrate capex after 2028

layers.name: Accelerators and compute silicon
layers.description: GPUs, custom ASICs, CPUs and inference chips.
layers.expansion_note: Units are capped upstream (N3, CoWoS, HBM); growth comes from performance per unit and price, and from custom silicon taking share.

risks.text: Customer concentration and $279bn of supply commitments; export controls and transition write-downs are disclosed risks
Hyperscaler custom silicon is ~1.9M of 6.5M units in 2026; Ironwood TCO estimated 44% below GB200
Rubin stated target 5.7M units but capped near 300k in 2026 by TSMC N3 capacity

watch: NVIDIA Q3 FY27 print (Nov 2026): $108bn guide, 71-72% gross margin

layers.name: Networking, interconnect and optics
layers.description: Switches, NICs, SerDes, optical transceivers and lasers that turn chips into clusters.
layers.expansion_note: Module makers can add lines within a year; EML lasers and InP wafers cannot, so the constraint sits upstream of the transceiver.

risks.text: EML laser and InP wafer shortages dictate 1.6T schedules; NVIDIA's $4bn lock-up of Lumentum and Coherent pushes other buyers past 2027
Chinese module makers hold 7 of the top 10 seats; tariffs and export controls are a policy risk to the whole optics chain
1.6T shortfalls likely through 2029; co-packaged optics and optical circuit switching could reroute value

watch: Lumentum and Coherent InP capacity statements

layers.name: Servers, racks, storage and cooling
layers.description: ODM/OEM systems, storage and liquid cooling that make clusters deployable.
layers.expansion_note: Assembly scales quickly in Taiwan and Mexico; liquid cooling and CDUs are the pinch, with Munters citing supply constraints.

risks.text: Rubin racks at 180-220 kW are fully liquid cooled with 3-6 MW CDUs; the 800VDC transition changes power-shelf suppliers
Supply constraints cost Munters SEK 300m in Q2 2026 despite orders +137%
ODM capacity is concentrated in Taiwan (Foxconn, Quanta, Wiwynn); tariffs and geopolitics move margins

layers.name: Data-centre electrical equipment and construction
layers.description: Transformers, switchgear, UPS, generators, cables and the EPC firms that build halls.
layers.expansion_note: Orders grow five times faster than capacity; backlogs lengthen rather than clear, and modular construction saves months, not years.

risks.text: Power transformer lead times 128 weeks, generator step-ups 144 weeks, prices +77% vs 2019
About half of planned 2026 US data-centre openings delayed or cancelled on transformer and switchgear shortages
GOES core steel is a five-firm oligopoly with only one US producer
Site work cannot be modularised; skilled electrical labour is the binding construction input

watch: Eaton and Siemens Energy backlog and book-to-bill

layers.name: Power generation and grid
layers.description: Turbines, fuel cells, nuclear, renewables, utilities and interconnection queues.
layers.expansion_note: Generation equipment grows ~9% a year against demand growing 60-160%; grid queues, moratoria and behind-the-meter gas decide who gets power first.

risks.text: Heavy-duty turbine lead times 3-7 years; three-firm oligopoly; prices +195% since 2019
ERCOT queue 474 GW (~90% data centres) with a ~2% request-to-operating funnel; Texas paused new data-centre connections on 3 Aug 2026
PJM capacity price rose 10x in two years; 116 municipal moratoria and New York's statewide pause
Energinet holds 33.5 GW of transmission connection requests (about 60 GW with distribution) against a 7 GW peak and signs no new large-load agreements before the autumn of 2026

watch: ERCOT large-load reports and the Texas audit
Energinet's first pooled capacity allocations (autumn 2026) and approval of its maturity method (due about 4 March 2027)

layers.name: Data centres
layers.description: Landlords, colocation, hyperscale self-build and crypto-site conversions delivering IT megawatts.
layers.expansion_note: 223 GW is in the global pipeline against ~25 GW under construction; delivery is gated by transformers, switchgear, permits and project finance.

risks.text: About 80% of data-centre securities issued since early 2025 trade wider than issue; two European bond deals pulled in July 2026
Single-tenant concentration: CoreWeave is ~100% of Core Scientific's colocation revenue and >76% of 2026E revenue
Crypto legacy drags converted sites (Hut 8's BTC and ABTC exposure, Bitdeer mining margins negative)
20+ projects cancelled in Q1 2026 ($41.7bn, 3.5 GW); public opposition 71% to a nearby data centre

layers.name: Compute providers
layers.description: Hyperscalers, neoclouds and in-house clusters selling or consuming GPU-hours.
layers.expansion_note: Capex grows 77% but delivered power grows slower; the difference shows up as rent, prepayments and debt at 6-10%.

risks.text: CoreWeave 5-year CDS 855bp (~50% implied default probability); $2.6bn loan forced to SOFR+550bp
Debt funds 32% of hyperscaler capex (from 9% in FY2024); Alphabet raised $84.75bn of equity and went FCF-negative
Customer concentration: CoreWeave customer A 40%, B 23%; Oracle cut to BBB- with FY27 FCF projected -$42bn
GPU rents are volatile: H100 fell 64-75% from the 2023 peak before rebounding 41%; a new generation resets prices

watch: SemiAnalysis H100 index and first GB300/Rubin one-year quotes

layers.name: Frontier labs and model providers
layers.description: Labs that turn GPU-hours into frontier and open-weight models.
layers.expansion_note: Compute and revenue grow together; the reflexive share (~43%) is the part of demand funded by the boom itself.

risks.text: About 43% of frontier-lab revenue is reflexive (coding, AI R&D, trading); a 10-point demand shock becomes 18 points in a bust
Gross margins 33% (OpenAI) to 40-50% (Anthropic) against targets of 70%+; compute commitments of 5-10 GW per lab must be serviced
Anthropic IPO targeted at $2T (19x exit-2026 run-rate); frontier-tier prices up ~100% since January while mid-tier fell 36%
EU AI Act transparency obligations live since Aug 2026, high-risk rules from Dec 2027

watch: Anthropic S-1 (late Sep 2026): gross margin, compute commitments, customer concentration

layers.name: Inference and distribution
layers.description: Inference clouds, aggregators and hyperscaler platforms that serve tokens.
layers.expansion_note: Token volume compounds while prices fall; value shifts to whoever routes and hosts open-weight models cheaply.

risks.text: Chinese open-weight models are ~46% of OpenRouter volume; open weights reach one-third of usage
Effective token prices fell 41% since March 2026 as buyers route volume away from the most expensive models (Ramp)
Seven serverless providers with a 6x price spread on the same model; consolidation under way (NVIDIA bought Groq assets for ~$20bn)

watch: OpenRouter weekly tokens and lab shares

layers.name: Token consumers
layers.description: Companies that buy tokens, split into unbounded and bounded tasks.
layers.expansion_note: Adoption is still widening but spend per seat at heavy users is softening; unbounded buyers keep paying for the frontier, bounded buyers route to the cheapest model.

risks.text: The 'SaaSpocalypse' erased ~$2T of software value Jan-Apr 2026; bounded-task incumbents face AI deflation (Infosys guidance cut to 1.5-3%)
AI-native startup token spend is funded by venture capital; a capital-markets freeze cuts frontier demand directly
Spend per seat at heavy users is softening even as adoption widens (Ramp, Aug 2026)
Jane Street lost ~$15bn in July 2026 partly via Situational Awareness LP; trading-firm token budgets are procyclical

layers.name: Capital providers
layers.description: Sovereign funds, private credit, banks, vendor finance and foundations that fund every layer.
layers.expansion_note: Issuance keeps rising ($334bn YTD) but secondary spreads say the marginal dollar is getting more expensive.

risks.text: JPMorgan estimates a $1.4T funding gap for the buildout; ~80% of data-centre securities trade wider than issue
Situational Awareness LP lost 67% in July 2026 on ~4x leverage and sold its public book to Citadel; levered AI vehicles are forced sellers
US 10-year at 4.97% and 30-year 5.35%; ECB and Nationalbank hiked in September 2026

nodes.name: Anthropic
nodes.sum: Leading frontier lab with $65bn run-rate (Jul 2026) and first operating profit; 43.5% of US businesses pay for its models. Claude Code alone is $15bn ARR, the single largest driver of reflexive coding demand.

nodes.name: Denmark data-centre capacity
nodes.sum: Denmark: 398 MW installed at start of 2026 with hyperscalers ~60%; Microsoft committed $3bn 2023-27; grid-connection pause halts expansion; data-centre electricity +17% in 2025 (2026).

nodes.name: Heavy-duty gas turbine market

bn.rationale: Orders exceed annual capacity 1.7x; hot-section castings do not scale on hyperscaler timelines

nodes.sum: Three-firm oligopoly manufacturing 60-70 GW/yr against ~110 GW outstanding orders; turbine prices +195% since 2019 to ~$600/kW; combined-cycle lead times 5-7 years (2026).

nodes.name: Amkor Technology
nodes.sum: Second-largest OSAT globally; advanced products 82% of Q2 2026 revenue (+27% y/y); building the first US high-volume advanced packaging facility in Arizona with $12bn investment and a 10-year TSMC partnership.

nodes.name: AT&S
nodes.sum: Europe's only top-tier IC substrate maker; doubled FY2026/27 capex to EUR 1.0-1.2bn after winning an AMD-backed Kulim expansion, guiding 45-55% revenue growth.

nodes.name: Behind-the-meter data-centre generation

cap.basis: on-site generation capacity announced or online

bn.rationale: Behind-the-meter is the marginal buyer's answer to a queue that adds firm capacity at roughly a fifth to a third of the announced buildout. It is a bridge while the queue clears, not a permanent substitute.

nodes.sum: About 2 GW of behind-the-meter data-centre generation is online mid-2026 against about 90 GW announced and 331 GW of disclosed grid-connected pipeline. SemiAnalysis expects it to power over half of new US data centres from 2028.

nodes.name: Global data-centre capacity and pipeline
nodes.sum: Global tracked capacity 86.8 GW; Americas 43.4 GW operational, 25.3 GW under construction, 191 GW pipeline; five facilities reach 1 GW in 2026; constrained by power and permitting (Q2 2026).

nodes.name: HBM market

bn.rationale: Three suppliers, wafer-intensive, allocated by NVIDIA

nodes.sum: Three-supplier oligopoly allocated by NVIDIA; HBM4 ~$550/stack vs $300 HBM3E; consumes 3-4x the wafer per bit of commodity DRAM, keeping supply constrained through end-2027.

nodes.name: Samsung Electro-Mechanics
nodes.sum: Samsung group FC-BGA and MLCC supplier; total quarterly revenue crossed KRW 3tn for the first time (KRW 3.21tn) while the package-substrate segment grew +45% y/y, winning NVIDIA as an FC-BGA customer and investing $1.2bn in Vietnam substrate lines.

nodes.name: SK hynix
nodes.sum: HBM market leader with ~50% revenue share in Q2 2026 (down from 62% a year earlier as Samsung and Micron gain); NVIDIA's primary HBM4 supplier, filing a US DRS for potential ADR listing.

nodes.name: US large-load (data-centre) interconnection queue

cap.basis: requested connection capacity, all data-centre projects

bn.rationale: The request stock is roughly three times the disclosed pipeline and more than five times the signed-agreement stock. Queue position is cheap to hold, so the headline is not demand; the credible pipeline is the 331 GW disclosed and the 195 GW committed.

nodes.sum: The US data-centre load queue: 1,066 GW requested, about 28 per cent likely to clear, 331 GW disclosed and 195 GW under signed agreements. It is the demand-side counterpart to the generation queue that clears about 2 per cent a year.

nodes.name: Micron
nodes.sum: Third HBM supplier with ~20% allocation; record fiscal Q3 revenue $41.5bn at 84.6% gross margin, with >$1bn HBM4 revenue and Idaho fab first-wafer mid-2027.

nodes.name: Nickel superalloys and turbine castings

bn.rationale: Four-firm oligopoly at capacity; single-crystal casting is extremely difficult to scale; gas turbine lead times 3-7 years; directly gates data centre power

nodes.sum: Only four companies worldwide cast gas-turbine blades at industrial scale; all at capacity in 2026. Single-crystal superalloy blades take years to manufacture and directly gate data-centre power delivery.

nodes.name: Samsung Electronics (memory and foundry)
nodes.sum: Projected mid-20% share of NVIDIA's HBM4 allocation and first challenger to ship HBM4 to NVIDIA, targeting doubled HBM shipments in 2027 - but on actual HBM revenue it sat third in Q2 2025 (17%) behind Micron (21%).

nodes.name: Large power transformers and switchgear

bn.rationale: GOES-constrained, 2-3 year lead times, price up 77%

nodes.sum: Power transformer lead times 128 weeks (vs ~40 in 2019), prices +77%; MV switchgear sold out through 2028. ~50% of planned 2026 US DC openings delayed on equipment shortages.

nodes.name: Helium supply (global)

bn.rationale: Qatar outage removed ~33% of global supply and the remaining capacity runs near-full; Exiger's source puts Ras Laffan recovery at 'a year or more' where equipment was damaged, and greenfield helium is 7-10 years away, so relief is 2028 at the earliest. Relief year moved from 2029 to 2028 on 2026-09-20 because the 3-5 year repair figure it rested on is not in the cited source

nodes.sum: Fab-grade helium with ~33% of global supply (Qatar's ~63 million cubic metres a year) offline since the March 2026 Ras Laffan strikes; spot prices doubled, greenfield takes 7-10 years, and no substitute exists for UHP helium in semiconductor manufacturing.

nodes.name: Linde
nodes.sum: Largest helium distributor with ~25% global share; Q2 2026 record sales $9.3bn (+9% YoY) with $8.1bn project backlog. Sells on-site recovery systems that cut fab helium consumption by 90-95%.

nodes.name: Air Products
nodes.sum: Second-largest helium supplier with ~15% global share; multiple US sources, Algerian and Qatari offtakes, and a Texas storage cavern. FY2026 helium caused ~4% EPS drag despite rising volumes.

nodes.name: Neon and specialty gases (lithography-grade)

bn.rationale: Ukraine war destroyed Mariupol capacity; China now dominant but quality variable; excimer/EUV lasers have no neon substitute

nodes.sum: Lithography-grade neon for DUV/EUV excimer lasers with no substitute; China's share rose to ~45% after Ukraine destroyed Mariupol capacity. Advanced EUV lines need 2-5x more neon per wafer.

nodes.name: Gallium (primary refined)

bn.rationale: Single-country supply under export control; suspensions expire Nov 2026; used in GaN/GaAs power and RF devices for 5G, radar, data centers

nodes.sum: China holds 99% of primary low-purity gallium (USGS 2025); its suspension of the US export ban runs out in November 2026 and prices rose over 200% during the 2024-25 controls. Critical feedstock for GaN power and RF devices in data centres.

nodes.name: Germanium (refined)

bn.rationale: China is the leading refiner, under export controls; critical for fiber optics and IR optics used in data center interconnects

nodes.sum: China is the leading refiner of germanium, under export controls; critical for fiber optics and infrared optics used in data-centre interconnects. Non-China recycling and zinc by-products supplement but cannot replace primary supply.

nodes.name: Indium (refined)

bn.rationale: China 69% of refined indium under Feb 2025 export controls; feedstock for InP substrates and ITO coatings critical to AI optical interconnects

nodes.sum: China refines 69% of global indium under February 2025 export controls; feedstock for InP substrates and ITO coatings critical to AI optical interconnects. Estimated 2025 output ~1,100 tonnes.

nodes.name: Rare earths (mined and separated)

bn.rationale: China 85-90% of separation and 90% of magnets; entity-specific bans on Western miners; magnets needed for HDD motors, wind turbines, robotics, EV motors

nodes.sum: China mines 68% of rare earths, controls 85-90% of separation, and makes ~90% of permanent magnets; April-October 2025 export controls remain partially in effect. Magnets needed for HDD motors, wind turbines and robotics.

nodes.name: MP Materials
nodes.sum: Largest US integrated rare-earth-to-magnet producer; record NdPr output 917 MT in Q1 2026 (+63% YoY) with $500M Apple magnet contract and $400M DoD equity stake. Scaling to 10,000 tpa by 2028.

nodes.name: Lynas Rare Earths
nodes.sum: Largest non-China separated rare earth producer with 7,337 tonnes NdPr in FY26 and a 12-year JARE agreement at US$110/kg floor. Revenue A$977.9M (+76% YoY); targeting full 10,500 tpa nameplate.

nodes.name: Indium phosphide (InP) wafers and epi

bn.rationale: 70% supply-demand gap gating 800G/1.6T optical transceivers; 3-supplier oligopoly; China export controls on indium and InP; 12-18 month lead times

nodes.sum: InP wafer supply-demand gap exceeds 70% in 2026, gating 800G/1.6T optical transceivers; top-3 suppliers hold >90% share with 12-18 month lead times. China export controls on indium add further risk.

nodes.name: AXT (Tongmei)
nodes.sum: ~35% of global InP substrates through Beijing Tongmei; record Q2 2026 revenue $47.6M (+164% YoY) with backlog above $100M. All manufacturing in China requires export permits; $87M in Lumentum prepayments secured.

nodes.name: High-purity quartz (Spruce Pine)

bn.rationale: Near-monopoly from one small US mining district; single points of failure (hurricane, fire, permitting); every silicon wafer depends on HPQ crucibles

nodes.sum: Spruce Pine, North Carolina provides 70-90% of high-purity quartz for semiconductor crucibles; operated by Sibelco and The Quartz Corp. Every silicon wafer depends on HPQ crucibles.

nodes.name: Grain-oriented electrical steel (GOES)

bn.rationale: Transformer cores need GOES; five-firm oligopoly with $500-700M entry cost; Cleveland-Cliffs only US producer; lead times 3-5 years

nodes.sum: Five-company oligopoly with 3.5-4 Mt combined GOES capacity; power transformer lead times stretched to 48-60 months. Only one US producer (Cleveland-Cliffs). Market $9.5bn in 2026.

nodes.name: Cleveland-Cliffs
nodes.sum: Sole US producer of high-silicon GOES with ~200,000 tpa capacity; secured $400M five-year DoD supply contract. Butler Works expansion adds +25% by 2028; Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA $286M.

nodes.name: Howmet Aerospace

cap.basis: global IGT turbine blade market share

nodes.sum: >50% global market share in industrial gas turbine blades; Q2 2026 revenue $2.55bn (+24% YoY) with gas-turbine segment +38%. Investing in new Japan, European and Virginia capacity.

nodes.name: Copper (data-centre and grid demand)

bn.rationale: AI data centres absorbing the entire annual growth in copper demand; Grasberg force majeure tightens supply; no new tier-one mines for years

nodes.sum: AI data centres consume 27-33 tonnes of copper per MW, absorbing roughly the entire annual growth in global demand. LME copper hit an all-time high in August 2026; Grasberg under force majeure.

nodes.name: SCHOTT (Zerodur)

cap.basis: derived from ASML shipments x mirrors per system

bn.rationale: Foundation-owned duopoly with Corning; mirror-blank lead times stretch with EUV ramp

nodes.sum: Foundation-owned maker of Zerodur glass-ceramic for EUV mirror substrates; duopoly with Corning, estimated ~55-60% of blanks. Revenue EUR 2.83bn (FY2024/25); acquired QSIL for quartz-glass capabilities.

nodes.name: Corning (ULE glass / Glass Innovations)
nodes.sum: Duopoly partner (with Schott) for ULE low-expansion glass used in EUV optics and mask blanks; also a major optical-fibre producer. Q1 2026 core sales $4.35bn (+18% YoY); Optical Communications +36%.

nodes.name: Ohara (Clearceram-Z)
nodes.sum: Third supplier of ultra-low-expansion glass for EUV mirror and photomask substrates via Clearceram-Z; smaller than Schott and Corning. Revenue Q3 2026 JPY 9.10bn (+25% YoY).

nodes.name: Hoya (EUV mask blanks)

cap.basis: share of global photomask blank market

bn.rationale: Duopoly with AGC; defect-free Mo/Si multilayer stacks are extraordinarily hard to produce

nodes.sum: 60%+ of global photomask blanks in a duopoly with AGC; an estimated 37-75% of EUV blanks specifically. Defect-free Mo/Si multilayer stacks are extraordinarily hard to produce; market growing at 13.5% CAGR.

nodes.name: Photronics
nodes.sum: Largest independent merchant photomask maker with ~10-14% market share; record high-end IC revenue in Q3 FY2026. Expanding EUV capabilities at Allen, Texas.

nodes.name: Mitsui Chemicals (EUV pellicles)

bn.rationale: CNT pellicles needed for High-NA EUV high-power sources; few qualified suppliers

nodes.sum: World's first commercial EUV pellicle producer under ASML licence; developing CNT-based pellicles with imec targeting >91% transmittance for High-NA EUV. Few qualified suppliers exist globally.

nodes.name: Wacker Chemie (polysilicon)
nodes.sum: Western world's largest polysilicon maker pivoting from solar to semiconductor-grade; new Burghausen etching line boosted semi-grade capacity >50%. FY2025 polysilicon segment EUR 883m.

nodes.name: Shin-Etsu Chemical

bn.rationale: Largest 300 mm supplier; no greenfield expansion announced; pricing discipline

nodes.sum: Largest 300 mm silicon wafer supplier with ~29% global capacity; no greenfield expansion announced, enforcing pricing discipline. Also building a dedicated EUV photoresist plant at Gunma (opened April 2026).

nodes.name: SUMCO

bn.rationale: No 2 wafer maker; operating losses despite strong demand signals pricing discipline and capacity restraint

nodes.sum: No. 2 in 300 mm wafers with ~24% global capacity; operating at a loss despite strong demand, signalling pricing discipline and capacity restraint. Q2 FY2026 guide JPY 112bn.

nodes.name: GlobalWafers

bn.rationale: Only large expansion plan in the top 5; Texas fab still ramping with heavy depreciation

nodes.sum: Only top-5 wafer maker with large-scale expansion; Sherman, Texas Phase 1 investing ~$3.5bn with a $500M Micron offtake agreement. ~15% of global 300 mm capacity.

nodes.name: Siltronic
nodes.sum: No. 4 in 300 mm wafers with ~12% capacity; EUR 2bn Singapore FabNext ramping but depressing margins with EUR 239m depreciation in H1 2026. AI's share of 300 mm rising from ~4% (2023) to ~12% (2026).

nodes.name: SK Siltron
nodes.sum: Korea's only 300 mm wafer maker, ~12% global capacity after July 2026 Gumi expansion (KRW 2.3tn invested). Primary customers Samsung and SK Hynix; potential Doosan acquisition advancing.

nodes.name: 300 mm silicon wafer market

bn.rationale: Incumbents refuse to over-expand after the last downcycle; LTAs rolling to higher prices

nodes.sum: Top five control ~92% of 300 mm capacity; market ~$10.3bn in 2026. Low-price LTAs expiring into a tightening market where AI servers consume 3.8x the wafer content of general servers.

nodes.name: Tokyo Ohka Kogyo (TOK)
nodes.sum: Top-5 photoresist maker producing EUV, KrF and 193i resists; vertically integrated from monomers. Building JPY 20bn Korea plant to serve Samsung; co-developing 2 nm resists with JSR.

nodes.name: JSR (incl. Inpria)

bn.rationale: Market leader now private; Taiwan plant not online until ~2028; 18-month qualification cycles

nodes.sum: Market leader (>22% share) in advanced photoresist, taken private by JIC at JPY 900bn; Inpria subsidiary develops metal-oxide EUV resist. Building Taiwan plant near TSMC (online ~2028) and Korea MOR plant (2026).

nodes.name: Fujifilm (semiconductor materials)
nodes.sum: ~15% photoresist share with a target to double semi materials to JPY 500bn by FY2030. Developed world's first PFAS-free ArF immersion resist (April 2026); also a leader in CMP slurries.

nodes.name: EUV photoresist market

bn.rationale: Japanese oligopoly with 18-month qualification cycles; metal-oxide resist adds complexity not relief

nodes.sum: Japanese suppliers hold ~80% of advanced photoresist with 18-month qualification cycles; market $5.5bn (2024) growing at >11% CAGR. Metal-oxide resists add chemistry complexity but not supply relief.

nodes.name: Ajinomoto (ABF build-up film)

bn.rationale: Sole-source dielectric film beneath every FCBGA accelerator package; 30% price hike + 30% China supply cut widens gap; next new capacity not until 2032

nodes.sum: >95% of ABF build-up film from two Japanese plants running at full capacity; announced 30% price hike and cut China supply 30% in 2026. Supply-demand gap projected to widen to 42% by 2028; next new plant not until 2032.

nodes.name: Nittobo (T-glass cloth)

bn.rationale: Sole-source glass cloth gates ABF substrate expansion; 10-20% shortage in 2026 widening before new capacity in mid-2027

nodes.sum: Effective sole source (~90%) of T-glass cloth for IC substrates; 10-20% shortage in 2026 widening before new capacity mid-2027. NVIDIA CEO visited to discuss supply; tripling capacity by 2028.

nodes.name: Entegris
nodes.sum: Leading supplier of CMP slurries, specialty gases and advanced deposition materials for sub-3 nm nodes; Q1 2026 sales $812m. Acquired CMC Materials (2022) to consolidate CMP position.

nodes.name: Merck KGaA (Semiconductor Solutions)
nodes.sum: Electronics segment supplies semiconductor materials and delivery systems for advanced fabs; Semiconductor Solutions organic growth +17.3% in Q2 2026. Full-year group guide EUR 21-21.8bn.

nodes.name: Semiconductor specialty gases market
nodes.sum: Five multinationals control >90% of semiconductor specialty gases ($5.04bn market in 2026); 6N purity now standard for CVD, etching and ion implantation at leading-edge nodes.

nodes.name: Carl Zeiss SMT

cap.basis: High-NA optic sets per year; low-NA optics output proxied by ASML EUV shipments (~65 in 2026)

bn.rationale: Single source; output measured in systems per year; no second supplier exists or can exist within a decade; ASML's own filing says the company would cease to function without Zeiss SMT

nodes.sum: Sole maker of EUV projection optics for every ASML scanner; ASML's own filing says the company would cease to function without Zeiss SMT. High-NA optics cadence flat since 2024; ASML bought EUR 4.41bn from Zeiss SMT in FY2025.

nodes.name: TRUMPF (EUV drive lasers)

cap.basis: drive-laser modules per year; 1:1 with ASML EUV systems

bn.rationale: One laser system per EUV tool; private company with no disclosed capacity; sole source; decade of co-development makes switching impossible

nodes.sum: Sole supplier of ~30 kW CO2 drive lasers for ASML's EUV sources; one laser per scanner with a decade of co-development making switching impossible. EUV division FY2024/25 revenue EUR 724m.

nodes.name: Cymer (ASML EUV source)

bn.rationale: In-house to ASML; source power is the throughput-limiting factor for EUV scanners

nodes.sum: ASML's in-house EUV light source business in San Diego; source power (~400 W) is the throughput-limiting factor for current scanners. High-NA targets 600-800 W to keep throughput above 200 wph.

nodes.name: VDL ETG (frames, vacuum, wafer handling)

bn.rationale: Private company; capacity must match ASML's ramp; limited visibility into output

nodes.sum: Supplies vacuum chambers and wafer-handling modules forming the mechanical backbone of each EUV scanner; part of the sole-source trio (Zeiss, TRUMPF, VDL) scaling with ASML's 2027-28 ramp. Privately held.

nodes.name: Lasertec (EUV mask inspection)

cap.basis: ACTIS actinic EUV mask inspection systems

bn.rationale: 100% market share in actinic EUV mask inspection; each additional EUV layer at N2/A14 adds inspection demand; A200HiT could multiply units per customer

nodes.sum: 100% global share in actinic EUV mask inspection; FY2026 revenue JPY 230.5bn (-8.3%) after orders collapsed ~60% in an air pocket before the A200HiT ramp, but still ahead of the JPY 200bn guide. KLA's competing tool significantly delayed.

nodes.name: Gigaphoton (DUV excimer lasers)

bn.rationale: DUV excimer lasers are a duopoly (Cymer/Gigaphoton); Gigaphoton supplies non-ASML DUV tools and replacement sources

nodes.sum: DUV excimer laser duopoly partner with Cymer (ASML), dominant in Asia; top three vendors hold ~86% of the ~$913m market. Subsidiary of Komatsu (6301.T).

nodes.name: ASML

bn.rationale: Sole EUV supplier; capacity rises 30% a year but a new tool still takes about two years from order to delivery; optics (Zeiss) gate the ramp

nodes.sum: Sole EUV lithography supplier with 100% share and >EUR 40bn backlog (~two-year waitlist); adding ~30% low-NA capacity for 2027. FY26 guide EUR 43-45bn; ~30x FY27 forward P/E.

nodes.name: Applied Materials

bn.rationale: Largest semicap equipment company; leading in deposition and etch for logic/DRAM; not sole-source but concentrated

nodes.sum: Largest semicap equipment company, leading in deposition and etch; Q2 FY2026 record revenue $7.91bn with 50% gross margin (highest in 25+ years). Raised CY2026 WFE growth outlook to >30%.

nodes.name: Lam Research

cap.basis: share of the etch equipment market; Lam's served-WFE share is in the mid-30s% and targeted at high-30s

bn.rationale: Dominant in etch (~50% share); critical for NAND high-aspect-ratio and GAA logic; but not sole-source

nodes.sum: Dominant in etch (~50% share), critical for NAND high-aspect-ratio and GAA logic; FY2026 record revenue $23.2bn (+30% YoY) with 52% gross margin. WFE outlook raised to low $150bn.

nodes.name: KLA Corporation

cap.basis: share of the process-control market; KLA is ~7.5% of total WFE and targets 9% by 2030

bn.rationale: Dominant in process control (7.5x nearest rival); rising complexity at N2/A14 and advanced packaging increases inspection intensity

nodes.sum: Dominant in process control at 7.5x the nearest rival; rising inspection intensity at N2/A14 drives demand. Advanced packaging process-control revenue growing ~70% to ~$1bn in 2026.

nodes.name: Tokyo Electron

cap.basis: Gartner/TechInsights market share data by product

bn.rationale: ~91% share in coater/developer is a near-monopoly; strong in etch (23%) and deposition (27%); critical for all leading-edge logic and memory

nodes.sum: ~91% share in coater/developer (near-monopoly), 23% etch, 27% deposition; FY2026 revenue JPY 2.44T with record net income JPY 574.4bn. Advanced packaging revenue to grow >60% in FY2027.

nodes.name: SCREEN Holdings

bn.rationale: Dominant in wet cleaning; second only to TEL among Japanese semicap peers; niche near-monopoly

nodes.sum: >45% global share in semiconductor wet cleaning equipment; FY2026 sales JPY 605.7bn; medium-term target JPY 1T. Niche near-monopoly in a process step required at every node.

nodes.name: Kokusai Electric

bn.rationale: 49-70% of batch deposition; critical for DRAM capacitor and NAND ALD layers; TEL is only competitor

nodes.sum: 49-70% of batch deposition (including ~70% of batch ALD); tier-1 supplier to all Big Five fabs. FY2026 revenue JPY 235.1bn; service revenue surged 127%.

nodes.name: Advantest

cap.basis: SoC and memory automated test equipment

bn.rationale: ~50% of SoC test and dominant in memory test; every NVIDIA GPU and every HBM chip is tested on Advantest equipment; 10x longer test time for AI chips creates capacity demand

nodes.sum: ~50% of SoC test and dominant in memory test; every NVIDIA GPU and HBM chip tested on Advantest equipment. AI chips need 10+ minutes vs <1 minute for smartphones; FY2026 guide raised to JPY 1,714bn.

nodes.name: Teradyne

bn.rationale: No. 2 in semiconductor test; AI and HBM demand driving 100%+ growth; capacity scaling required

nodes.sum: No. 2 in semiconductor test (~35% SoC share); Q2 2026 revenue $1.33bn (+104% YoY) with AI ~70% of revenue. Semi Test segment grew 128% to $1.12bn.

nodes.name: BE Semiconductor (hybrid bonding)

bn.rationale: Dominant in hybrid bonding for advanced packaging; technology qualification for HBM could multiply demand; 2027 adoption = potential hockey stick

nodes.sum: ~80% share in hybrid bonding for advanced packaging; 21 customers with record orders in Q1-Q2 2026. Hybrid-bonded HBM stacks in qualification; volume memory adoption is a 2027+ catalyst. Stock -41% from peak.

nodes.name: Hanmi Semiconductor

cap.basis: TC bonder units for HBM manufacturing

bn.rationale: 71% of HBM TC bonders; each HBM generation transition causes order lumpiness; hybrid bonding is a longer-term displacement risk

nodes.sum: 71.2% of global HBM TC bonder market (TechInsights); SK hynix placed first HBM4 Griffin order in June 2026. Q2 2026 record revenue KRW 251.1bn with 51.9% operating margin.

nodes.name: Disco Corporation

bn.rationale: Near-monopoly in dicing and grinding; HBM wafer thinning is a critical step that only Disco's tools can reliably achieve at scale

nodes.sum: 70-80% share in precision dicing and grinding; near-monopoly in HBM wafer thinning to 30-50 um that only Disco's tools can reliably achieve at scale. FY2026 revenue JPY 436.9bn (+11.1%).

nodes.name: ASMPT (ASM Pacific Technology)

cap.basis: die bonders, wire bonders, TC bonders, hybrid bonders

bn.rationale: Broad packaging-equipment portfolio; growing rapidly in TCB for AI; 5.6% HBM TC share growing

nodes.sum: Broad packaging-equipment portfolio growing rapidly in TC bonding for AI; H1 2026 bookings surged 85.1% to $1.63bn with book-to-bill 1.43. Computer applications now 33% of revenue (from 10% in 2024).

nodes.name: Onto Innovation

bn.rationale: Growing challenger to KLA in advanced packaging process control; Dragonfly G5 ramp is a share-gain catalyst

nodes.sum: Growing challenger to KLA in advanced packaging process control; record Q2 2026 revenue $343m (+35% YoY). Dragonfly G5 qualified at a leading 2.5D logic customer; HBM inspection seeing phenomenal growth.

nodes.name: ASM International (ALD)

bn.rationale: Leader in single-wafer ALD for leading-edge logic and memory; GAA/CFET demand drives tool intensity

nodes.sum: Leader in single-wafer ALD for leading-edge logic and memory; GAA/CFET architectures drive rising tool intensity. Q2 2026 revenue +24% YoY with 33% adjusted operating margin.

nodes.name: 300 mm fab equipment spending
nodes.sum: Market segment tracking 300 mm fab equipment spending: $133bn in 2026 (+18%), $151bn in 2027; multiple vendors now estimate CY2026 WFE in the low $150bn range.

nodes.name: TSMC

bn.rationale: Effectively sole leading-edge AI logic foundry; N3 sold out, N2 booked to 2028

nodes.sum: Sole leading-edge AI logic foundry with ~90% share of N3/N2; Q2 2026 revenue $40.2bn (+34% y/y) at 67.7% gross margin, with $60-64bn capex and packaging, not wafers, as the binding constraint.

nodes.name: Intel Foundry
nodes.sum: Only western alternative to TSMC for leading-edge logic; first production High-NA EXE:5200B for 14A node, but foundry still loss-making and years from AI-volume relevance.

nodes.name: Global 300 mm fab capacity
nodes.sum: Total 300 mm capacity forecast at 9.6M wafers a month in 2026; China 25%, Korea 23%, Taiwan 21%. The segment carries the dashboard's fab capacity series, but the forecast is from a 2023 SEMI outlook and has not been refreshed.

nodes.name: CXMT (ChangXin Memory)
nodes.sum: China's largest DRAM maker; HBM allocation growing from ~1% (2025) to ~12% by 2028, with potential to flood commodity DRAM and compress incumbents' margins.

nodes.name: Sandisk (NAND)
nodes.sum: Largest independent NAND supplier; fiscal Q4 2026 revenue $9.0bn (+51% q/q) with eight NBM agreements covering ~50% of FY27 bits, locking in AI data-centre storage demand.

nodes.name: TSMC CoWoS

bn.rationale: Sole source for NVIDIA, AMD and Broadcom accelerators; gap closing but not closed

nodes.sum: Sole advanced-packaging path for NVIDIA, AMD and Broadcom accelerators; capacity rises from 77.5k to ~130k wafers a month during 2026 against ~1.0M wafers of demand for the year, and TSMC's own management says packaging, not wafer starts, is what limits customers' growth.

nodes.name: ASE Technology (OSAT)
nodes.sum: World's largest OSAT; LEAP advanced-packaging revenue >$3.7bn in 2026 doubling to $7.5bn+ in 2027, with record $10.5bn capex signalling packaging as the constraint.

nodes.name: SPIL (ASE subsidiary)
nodes.sum: Key ASE subsidiary and major NVIDIA packaging supplier; aggressively acquiring factory space in 2026 (Nanke, Hsinchu, Yunlin) to expand 2.5D/3D advanced packaging capacity.

nodes.name: Ibiden (ABF substrates)
nodes.sum: Largest IC package substrate maker; FY2025 electronics revenue Y243bn (+23% y/y) at 18.6% OPM; Y500bn capex FY2026-28 targeting 2.8x AI substrate capacity by 2028.

nodes.name: Unimicron (ABF substrates)
nodes.sum: Taiwan's largest ABF substrate maker; Q2 2026 revenue NT$42.9bn (+32% y/y) with ABF 52% of revenue at >90% utilization; $1.4bn GDS raised to fund AI substrate expansion.

nodes.name: Kinsus (Pegatron)
nodes.sum: Pegatron subsidiary and top-5 ABF substrate maker; July 2026 revenue NT$4.55bn (+36% y/y), fifth consecutive record; NT$19.6bn additional capex approved for expansion.

nodes.name: Nan Ya PCB
nodes.sum: Formosa Plastics group substrate maker; Q1 2026 revenue NT$11.2bn (+32% y/y); capex >NT$10bn in largest-ever expansion as management warns ABF supply-demand gap widens through 2028.

nodes.name: ABF substrate market

bn.rationale: Utilization >95%, 26-week lead times, sole-source film and glass cloth upstream

nodes.sum: ABF substrates are the bottleneck below CoWoS: >95% utilization, 26-week lead times, and orders secured to 2029-30 in 2026; packaging costs up 18-25%.

nodes.name: NVIDIA
nodes.sum: Dominant GPU maker with ~70% of 2026 AI accelerator spend (a much smaller share of units, which custom silicon now takes ~1.9M of). Q2 FY27 revenue $96.2bn with Data Center at $89.0bn (+117% y/y), 75.0% gross margin and $279bn of supply commitments make its earnings the buildout's demand pulse.

nodes.name: AMD
nodes.sum: Second-largest discrete GPU maker; MI450 Helios racks shipping Q3 2026 with anchor customers Meta and OpenAI (6 GW agreement). The closest merchant-silicon alternative to NVIDIA (2026).

nodes.name: Broadcom
nodes.sum: Primary custom ASIC partner for Google TPU (supply agreement through 2031) and OpenAI Jalapeño. Q3 FY26 AI semiconductor revenue $16.7bn (+221% y/y); ~$29bn residual-value backstop from Google (2026).

nodes.name: Google TPU (Ironwood / TPU8)
nodes.sum: Google's in-house accelerator; Ironwood at 4.3M projected 2026 units offers estimated TCO ~44% below GB200. Up to 1M units committed to Anthropic across 3.5 GW of capacity (2026).

nodes.name: AWS Trainium
nodes.sum: Amazon's custom training chip with >1M processors deployed. Anthropic targets ~1 GW of Trainium in 2026 within a 5 GW AWS collaboration, making it the second custom-silicon path after TPU.

nodes.name: Cerebras
nodes.sum: Wafer-scale inference chip maker; raised $5.5bn in the largest tech IPO of 2026. Delivers ~1,700 tokens/s on gpt-oss-120B, positioning it as a high-throughput inference alternative to NVIDIA.

nodes.name: AI accelerator shipments
nodes.sum: Tracks ~6.5M data-centre AI accelerator units in 2026 across NVIDIA, AMD, Intel and custom silicon, with ~1.9M units from hyperscaler ASICs (TPU, Trainium, Maia, MTIA).

nodes.name: Arista Networks
nodes.sum: Leading data-centre switch vendor; Q2 2026 revenue $3.04bn (+38%) with 1.6 Tbps AI fabric platforms. Merchant-silicon dependency and hyperscaler customer concentration are disclosed risks (2026).

nodes.name: Credo (AECs, SerDes, optical DSP)
nodes.sum: Designs active electrical cables and SerDes for 1.6T interconnect; Q1 FY27 revenue $479M (+115% y/y) at 27x forward P/E. The 1.6T AEC ramp in H2 FY27 is the next catalyst.

nodes.name: Coherent
nodes.sum: One of three EML laser makers (with Lumentum and DSBJ) that dictate 1.6T transceiver schedules. FQ4 2026 datacenter revenue $1.6bn; InP supply-demand gap is the binding constraint (2026).

nodes.name: Lumentum

bn.rationale: EML lasers and InP wafers are the binding input for 800G/1.6T

nodes.sum: EML laser and InP photonics maker; NVIDIA committed $4bn to Lumentum and Coherent for priority access, pushing other buyers past 2027. CEO says InP gap exceeds DRAM and NAND (2026).

nodes.name: Innolight
nodes.sum: World's largest optical transceiver maker at 23.4% market share (LightCounting #1, 2025); 800G capacity ~14.5M units. Core supplier to Google and Microsoft with 1.6T OSFP-XD in production (2026).

nodes.name: AI optical transceiver market

bn.rationale: EML and InP upstream; Chinese module makers hold 7 of top 10 seats

nodes.sum: AI optical transceiver market growing from $16.5bn (2025) to $26bn (2026); 800G production 40-60% below demand through 2027. EML lasers and InP wafers are the upstream bottleneck.

nodes.name: Vertiv
nodes.sum: Leading thermal and power infrastructure supplier; FY26 net sales guided to $13.8-14.2bn at 31% organic growth, Q2 sales $3,274m (+24%). Content per MW rising from ~$3.5m to ~$7m on full-stack modular designs, and it is buying UtilityInnovation Group to sell behind-the-meter power as well (2026).

nodes.name: Munters
nodes.sum: Swedish air-treatment and DC cooling specialist; Q2 2026 orders +137% with 3.6x data-centre book-to-bill. Supply constraints cost SEK 300M in Q2 despite backlog SEK 24.5bn (+151%) (2026).

nodes.name: Alfa Laval
nodes.sum: Swedish heat-exchanger maker; Q2 2026 orders SEK 22bn (+35%) with order book SEK 53.5bn. Data-centre cooling ~SEK 5bn/yr; doubling Virginia capacity by 2028 (2026).

nodes.name: Danfoss
nodes.sum: Foundation-owned Danish maker of compressors, heat exchangers, valves and drives for data-centre cooling; data-centre sales about 7% of EUR 9.43bn and almost doubling in 2025. The largest Danish supplier into the physical chain that earlier builds missed (2026).

nodes.name: Grundfos
nodes.sum: Foundation-owned Danish pump maker whose chilled-water and liquid-cooling pumps sit inside data-centre cooling loops; names data centres a key growth driver of EUR 4.7bn of 2025 revenue (2026).

nodes.name: Data-centre liquid cooling market
nodes.sum: Data-centre liquid cooling market at $4.1bn in 2026, growing to $27.7bn by 2033. Rubin racks at 180-220 kW are fully liquid cooled, making CDUs the fastest-growing component.

nodes.name: Eaton
nodes.sum: Leading electrical equipment maker; Q2 2026 Electrical Americas orders +41%, backlog +43% at 1.4x book-to-bill. Eaton's orders data is the fastest electrical-demand pulse for the buildout (2026).

nodes.name: Siemens Energy
nodes.sum: Top-4 global transformer OEM with record grid backlog EUR 51bn; expanding transformer capacity 50% by 2030 with $1bn US investment. Gas turbine backlog 69 GW at fiscal Q3 2026.

nodes.name: Schneider Electric
nodes.sum: French electrical and software group; H1 2026 organic +14% with triple-digit DC and semiconductor demand growth (>24% of revenue). Acquired Motivair for liquid cooling CDUs (2026).

nodes.name: Prysmian
nodes.sum: World's largest cable maker; transmission backlog EUR 17bn. FY26 EBITDA guide raised to EUR 2.8-2.9bn; Digital Solutions (DC and fibre cables) +18% at 23.8% margin (2026).

nodes.name: NKT
nodes.sum: Only listed Danish company in the AI supply chain and a European grid play; Transmission backlog EUR 13.0bn at 30 June 2026 (EUR 11.6bn at standard metal prices), excluding over EUR 2.5bn of TenneT framework awards. FY26 EBITDA guide EUR 400-430M; net cash (2026).

nodes.name: Sterling Infrastructure
nodes.sum: US e-infrastructure contractor; Q2 2026 revenue $1.17bn (+90%) with e-infrastructure 78% of total. Signed backlog $4.33bn at 1.4x book-to-bill (2026).

nodes.name: Comfort Systems USA
nodes.sum: US mechanical and electrical contractor for modular data centres; backlog $14.06bn at 30 Jun 2026, up from $12.45bn a quarter earlier and $8.12bn a year earlier, on Q2 revenue of $3.27bn. Modular construction cuts capex/MW ~8% and schedules ~36% (2026).

nodes.name: GE Vernova
nodes.sum: Largest gas turbine maker: gas equipment backlog and slot reservations 116 GW, up from 100 GW in Q1 and 83 GW at end-2025, against ~20 GW/yr of output rising to 24 GW in 2028; $176bn total backlog, Q2 orders $24.2bn (+88% organic) and over $5bn of data-centre orders year to date, more than double all of 2025 (Q2 2026).

nodes.name: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (gas turbines)
nodes.sum: Second in the three-firm heavy-duty turbine oligopoly; large-frame backlog 35 GW, up 52% y/y; intends to double capacity by fiscal 2030 (Aug 2026).

nodes.name: Bloom Energy
nodes.sum: On-site fuel-cell supplier bypassing grid queues for data centres; record Q2 2026 results with raised FY26 guidance; market cap $74bn (Sep 2026).

nodes.name: ERCOT (Texas grid)

bn.rationale: Phantom-load queue; approvals are ~2% of requests; political pause

nodes.sum: Texas grid with 474 GW large-load requests (~90% data centres) against ~3.9 GW approved; Governor paused new data-centre connections 3 Aug 2026; 198 GW applied in Q1 alone (Aug 2026).

nodes.name: PJM Interconnection
nodes.sum: Eastern US grid: capacity price 10x in two years ($329/MW-day), interconnection waits up to 7 years in Northern Virginia; projected 6.6 GW deficit by 2027-28 (Sep 2026).

nodes.name: US generation interconnection queues (LBNL)
nodes.sum: National generation queue: 1,312 GW active requests across ~8,200 projects; gas +86% to 253 GW; median request-to-operation >5 years with only 13% historically completing (2025).

nodes.name: Energinet (Danish TSO)

bn.rationale: Transmission requests alone are about 5x the national peak and about 60 GW with distribution is 8-9x; no new agreements before the autumn of 2026 turns Denmark from cheap-power host into a constrained market

nodes.sum: Danish TSO: 33.5 GW of transmission connection requests (about 60 GW with distribution) against a 7 GW national peak; no new large-load agreements before the autumn of 2026, pooled handling under maturity criteria that the regulator has frozen until approved (Sep 2026).

nodes.name: Core Scientific
nodes.sum: Crypto miner turned landlord: 590 MW leased to CoreWeave and 529 MW on the AMD/neocloud agreements (377 MW direct AMD) on 12-15 year take-or-pay terms; 437 MW billing by mid-July. CoreWeave is over 76% of 2026 revenue with no disclosed credit enhancement, so its credit is the risk (Q2 2026).

nodes.name: Applied Digital
nodes.sum: GPU-ready landlord: 1,410 MW leased at $36.2bn base-term; 175 MW live, ~810 MW unfunded requiring $8-12bn; FY26 revenue $611m (+167%) with 91% NOI margin but 36% SBC (FY26).

nodes.name: TeraWulf
nodes.sum: Bitcoin miner pivoting to AI: 401 MW signed with Anthropic for 20 years (~$19bn) but with the credit support behind that contract still unsigned as of Jul 2026; Google $3.2bn backstop covers the separate Fluidstack lease at Lake Mariner. 102 MW live, scaling to 336+ MW by 2027 (Jul 2026).

nodes.name: Cipher Mining
nodes.sum: Crypto-to-AI landlord: 493 IT MW contracted (700 MW headline is gross); Black Pearl leased to Amazon Data Services with an Amazon.com parent guarantee (AA); Barber Lake leased to Fluidstack with a Google $1.73bn backstop plus 24M warrants; project bonds Ba3/BB-, not investment grade (Jul 2026).

nodes.name: Hut 8
nodes.sum: Largest crypto-conversion pipeline: 949 MW contracted at $26.6bn base-term; first single-sponsor data-centre IG bond ($3.25bn, BBB); Alphabet backstop at River Bend (Jul 2026).

nodes.name: IREN
nodes.sum: Australian-listed AI landlord: Microsoft 200 MW at $9.7bn over 5 years; new contracts >$20m/IT MW; NVIDIA right to invest $2.1bn tied to GPU delivery; $1bn operating ARR (Aug 2026).

nodes.name: Bitdeer
nodes.sum: Singapore-based miner: Tydal 121 IT MW lease to Volta ($4.7bn over 16 years, ~90% NOI margin) whose headline rent is a 16-year average, leaving year-one NOI ~$207m; tenant can walk at year ten and the $1.3bn LC backstop is still conditional. Only 2.5 MW of AI live versus 1,752 MW of total electrical capacity (Aug 2026).

nodes.name: Equinix

cap.basis: estimated IT load, mostly non-AI colocation

nodes.sum: World's largest colocation provider: 281 data centres in 77 markets, ~2 GW estimated IT load, ~3 GW developable; $99bn market cap; primarily enterprise interconnection (Jul 2026).

nodes.name: Digital Realty

cap.basis: estimated IT load, mostly non-AI colocation

nodes.sum: Second-largest colocation provider: ~2.5 GW estimated IT load; record 200 MW Charlotte lease Apr 2026; hosts the Danish Gefion DGX SuperPOD in Copenhagen; $71bn market cap (Jul 2026).

nodes.name: Amazon (AWS)
nodes.sum: Largest cloud provider: AWS Q2 revenue $42.2bn (+37%), $496bn backlog (6.4-year average life), $200-220bn 2026 capex; ~10 GW live, capacity likely insufficient through 2027. Long-term debt doubled to $128.9bn in six months and the Anthropic stake is now carried above $190bn (Q2 2026).

nodes.name: Microsoft (Azure)
nodes.sum: Second-largest cloud: $175bn calendar-2026 capex, $678bn commercial RPO (+84%, OpenAI ~45%); Microsoft Cloud revenue $59.3bn in the quarter; ~6 GW live after adding 31 data centres and 1 GW in FQ4; paused 2-3.5 GW of future builds (Q2 2026).

nodes.name: Alphabet (Google Cloud)
nodes.sum: Third-largest cloud: Q2 revenue $24.8bn (+82%), $514bn backlog, $200bn 2026 capex; raised $84.75bn equity (largest on record); first negative-FCF quarter since IPO (Q2 2026).

nodes.name: Meta Platforms
nodes.sum: Largest in-house compute builder: $130-145bn 2026 capex, ~5.5 GW live heading to >10 GW; Q2 revenue $60.8bn (+28%); $349bn of non-cancelable commitments and $83.7bn of long-term debt after a $25bn May issue (Q2 2026).

nodes.name: Oracle (OCI)
nodes.sum: Stargate host and aggressive cloud entrant: 1.8 GW live including 1.2 GW Abilene; CDS 215bp, BBB-/Baa2 negative; FY27 FCF projected -$42bn; stock -54% from one-year high (Sep 2026).

nodes.name: CoreWeave
nodes.sum: Largest neocloud: Q2 revenue $2.6bn (+112%), $104bn backlog, 1.5 GW active of ~3.7 GW contracted; 5-year CDS 855bp (~50% implied default); $35.1bn debt plus $16.3bn of operating leases; customer A (Microsoft) 40% of revenue (Q2 2026).

nodes.name: Nebius
nodes.sum: Yandex-successor neocloud: Q2 revenue $582m (+454%), $3bn ARR; 800 MW-1 GW by YE2026; deals at $20-25m/MW-yr; >$9bn prepayments expected; $5.75bn converts closed Aug 2026 (Q2 2026).

nodes.name: SpaceX / xAI (Colossus)
nodes.sum: Musk AI compute arm: 1.4 GW nameplate scaling to >2 GW YE2026 and ~10 GW by 2027; Anthropic rents Colossus 1+2 at up to $15bn/yr; acquired Cursor for $60bn in shares (Q2 2026).

nodes.name: GPU rental market (H100 index)
nodes.sum: H100 one-year rents rose 41% Oct 2025-Apr 2026 while Blackwell shipped; Sep 2026 spot B300 $7-18/hr; most compute transacts below $20m/MW-yr, fast capacity $30-50m (Sep 2026).

nodes.name: Big-4 hyperscaler capex
nodes.sum: Big-4 capex: $150bn (2023) to $410bn (2025) to guided $725bn (2026); debt funds 32% vs 9% in FY2024; $334bn data-centre bond/loan issuance 2026 YTD (Sep 2026).

nodes.name: OpenAI
nodes.sum: Frontier lab with $40bn run-rate (Jul 2026); Codex generates 64% of combined enterprise output tokens. Cash burn $27bn in 2026 with $63bn planned for 2027, funded by massive compute commitments from Azure, AWS and NVIDIA.

nodes.name: Google DeepMind (Gemini)
nodes.sum: Alphabet subsidiary operating Gemini models with an estimated $30bn exit-2026 run-rate; Google Cloud deals carry 90-day cancellation clauses, making its demand the most elastic among the top three labs.

nodes.name: xAI (Grok)
nodes.sum: Elon Musk's AI lab running Grok on the 200k-GPU Colossus cluster; reached 4.0% of US businesses in Jul 2026. Leased Colossus 1 to Anthropic, suggesting internal demand trails capacity.

nodes.name: Meta Superintelligence Labs
nodes.sum: Meta's in-house frontier lab; Prometheus reached 1 GW in May 2026 with Hyperion planned at 2-5 GW. Open-weight Llama models drive ~46% of OpenRouter volume but Meta captures no direct token revenue.

nodes.name: DeepSeek
nodes.sum: Chinese frontier lab whose V4 Flash handles >619bn tokens/day on OpenRouter (Aug 2026); trained V3 for ~$5.6m. Open-weight models commoditise inference and are ~46% of OpenRouter volume.

nodes.name: Frontier-lab revenue pool
