dc.why: Danish-founded; AI resolution pricing at $1.50; bounded per-ticket tasks

nodes.sum: Danish-founded customer-support SaaS with three-tier AI resolution model at $1.50/resolution (May 2026). Bounded/short, boom-funded share 0.00: outcome-based pricing means cheapest adequate model wins.

nodes.name: Intercom

dc.why: Fin AI agent for customer support; published pricing comparison vs Zendesk and Agentforce

nodes.sum: Customer-support platform with Fin AI agent for automated resolution. Bounded/short, boom-funded share 0.00: per-resolution market where frontier models are unnecessary and prices converge to cost.

nodes.name: Teleperformance

dc.why: AI LOSER: 500k employees; targeting all using AI tools by end-2026; revenue growth just 0-2%; Klarna disclosure triggered 29% selloff

nodes.sum: World's largest contact center (500k employees); revenue -2.2% LFL, short interest rose from 3.8% to 12%, fwd PE 4.9x. Bounded/short, boom-funded share 0.00: canonical AI-deflated BPO name.

nodes.name: Concentrix

dc.why: AI LOSER: cut FY26 revenue outlook by $130M; stock -25%; clients moving work offshore faster or ditching support entirely

nodes.sum: Contact center that cut FY26 revenue by ~$130m; fwd PE 2.3x. Bounded/short, boom-funded share 0.00: clients cutting call-center spending as AI replaces tasks directly.

nodes.name: Accenture

dc.why: $3bn committed to GenAI; 77k AI professionals; but FY26 growth only 3-5% as large-deal conversion softens

nodes.sum: IT consulting giant with $2.2bn advanced AI bookings (+76%) in Q1 FY26 and $4.8bn cumulative AI revenue; 77k AI professionals. Bounded/short, boom-funded share 0.00: growth only 3-5%.

nodes.name: Tata Consultancy Services

dc.why: Aims to be 'largest AI-led firm'; $2.6bn AI revenue; but core IT services face AI deflation

nodes.sum: Indian IT services with $2.6bn annualised AI revenue run-rate and $9.5bn order book (Q1 FY27). Bounded/short, boom-funded share 0.00: core services face AI deflation despite growing AI bookings.

nodes.name: Ramp

dc.why: AI-first corporate card and expense management; publishes the AI Index tracking 70k businesses

nodes.sum: AI-first corporate card that publishes the Ramp AI Index tracking AI adoption across 70,000 US businesses monthly. Bounded/short, boom-funded share 0.00: its spending data is the graph's primary adoption indicator.

nodes.name: Marvell Technology
nodes.sum: Primary custom silicon partner for AWS (Trainium/Graviton) and Microsoft (Maia); data centre >70% of revenue. Q2 FY27 custom silicon +88% y/y makes it the leading independent ASIC design house.

nodes.name: Alchip Technologies
nodes.sum: Taiwanese ASIC turnkey provider at TSMC 3 nm/CoWoS; key design partner for Broadcom's TPU programme. 2026 revenue guided +40-50% y/y at a 28% gross margin typical of the turnkey model.

nodes.name: MediaTek
nodes.sum: Taiwanese chip designer building Google TPU 8i (inference variant) at TSMC 2 nm for late 2027, adding a second design source alongside Broadcom for Google's custom silicon roadmap.

nodes.name: Intel (Gaudi / Xeon)
nodes.sum: Legacy chipmaker with Gaudi 3 at 80-120k units in 2026, well below NVIDIA/AMD scale. Intel Foundry posted $0.5bn Q2 operating loss while ramping 18A; restructuring cuts 15k jobs.

nodes.name: Huawei Ascend
nodes.sum: China's primary AI accelerator under US export controls; Ascend 910C ships to Alibaba, Baidu and Tencent at an estimated 200-300k units in 2026 on SMIC 7 nm.

nodes.name: Arm Holdings
nodes.sum: Sole-source ISA for every major hyperscaler custom chip (Trainium, Graviton, Axion, Maia, MTIA). Q1 FY27 royalty +23% as v9 AI cores raise the per-chip royalty rate (2026).

nodes.name: Microsoft Maia
nodes.sum: Microsoft's in-house inference ASIC; Maia 100 (5 nm) deployed in Azure since late 2024, Maia 200 (3 nm) in production for 2026-27, reducing NVIDIA dependence for internal workloads.

nodes.name: Meta MTIA
nodes.sum: Meta's in-house accelerator for ranking and recommendation inference; MTIA v2 on 5 nm deployed, v3 at 3 nm for 2026-27 training, supplementing NVIDIA GPUs and AMD MI450.

nodes.name: Astera Labs
nodes.sum: Designs PCIe 6.0 retimers and CXL smart cables for NVIDIA GB200/Rubin platforms; Q2 2026 revenue $201M (+176% y/y) at 75% gross margin. Top customer >40% of revenue (2026).

nodes.name: Cisco Systems
nodes.sum: Second-largest data-centre switch maker; Silicon One G200 for 400G/800G spine. AI infrastructure orders exceeded $5bn in FY26 with Q4 revenue $14.4bn (2026).

nodes.name: Ciena
nodes.sum: WaveLogic 6 Extreme coherent optics at 1.6T per wavelength for DC interconnect; Q3 FY26 revenue $1.22bn (+18%) with DCI revenue growing >30% y/y as AI clusters span metros (2026).

nodes.name: Amphenol
nodes.sum: Dominant supplier of high-speed copper and optical interconnects to GPU racks; IT datacom +65% y/y, now >35% of Q2 2026 revenue ($5.16bn). Content per rack rises with each GPU generation.

nodes.name: TE Connectivity
nodes.sum: High-speed backplane connectors and cable assemblies for AI server racks; content per rack rising from ~$500 to >$2,000 on Rubin. Q3 FY26 Data & Devices +28% y/y (2026).

nodes.name: Eoptolink
nodes.sum: Second-largest Chinese transceiver maker behind Innolight; 800G OSFP in volume, 1.6T in qualification. Key supplier to Microsoft and Meta within China's 60% share of global module production (2026).

nodes.name: NVIDIA Networking (NVLink / Spectrum-X)
nodes.sum: NVLink 6 delivers 3.6 TB/s per GPU in Rubin racks for all-to-all within-rack communication; Spectrum-X provides 800G Ethernet for multi-rack. Networking revenue estimated $15-18bn in FY27 (2026).

nodes.name: Corning Optical Communications
nodes.sum: Corning's optical fibre segment; Q2 2026 revenue $1.47bn (+38%) on AI-optimised single-mode fibre and ClearCurve for intra-DC cabling. Multi-year hyperscaler agreements secure volume (2026).

nodes.name: Fabrinet
nodes.sum: Thai-based contract manufacturer; NVIDIA at ~30% and Lumentum at ~15% of revenue for transceiver and switch assembly. Q4 FY26 revenue $980M (+25%); optical comms ~75% of total (2026).

nodes.name: Foxconn / Hon Hai Precision
nodes.sum: World's largest EMS and a top-3 NVIDIA GB200/GB300 rack integrator. Q2 2026 revenue ~$55bn; AI server >30% of total. Diversifying assembly to Mexico and India from China (2026).

nodes.name: Quanta Computer
nodes.sum: Top-3 NVIDIA rack integrator; also builds for Google (TPU) and Microsoft. AI/cloud server ~55% of Q2 2026 revenue; TWSE monthly revenue shows >40% y/y growth since January 2026.

nodes.name: Wiwynn
nodes.sum: Taiwanese ODM that integrates GPU racks; roughly half of revenue depends on Microsoft, so its monthly TWSE revenue is the fastest public read on Azure's AI build. Q2 2026 +65% y/y.

nodes.name: Super Micro Computer
nodes.sum: US-based liquid-cooled rack leader with fastest time-to-market for new NVIDIA platforms. Q4 FY26 revenue $5.7bn (+45%) at 12% gross margin; auditor issues resolved in early 2026.

nodes.name: Dell Technologies
nodes.sum: Largest enterprise server OEM; AI server backlog $6.8bn, up from $3.8bn a year ago. PowerEdge GB200 and GB300 racks shipping; ISG AI-optimised servers >40% of ISG revenue (Q2 FY27).

nodes.name: Hewlett Packard Enterprise
nodes.sum: Enterprise server and HPC vendor; AI system backlog ~$5.5bn on ProLiant and Cray EX platforms. Q3 FY26 Server +30%; GreenLake as-a-service shifts the revenue model (2026).

nodes.name: Seagate Technology
nodes.sum: Top-2 HDD maker; Mozaic 3+ HAMR drives (30 TB+) ship to hyperscalers for AI training data and checkpointing. Q4 FY26 revenue $2.31bn at 36% gross margin; exabyte shipments +25% y/y (2026).

nodes.name: Western Digital
nodes.sum: Top-2 HDD maker post-Sandisk spin-off; UltraSMR 32 TB drives for AI cloud storage. Q4 FY26 Cloud revenue +42%; competes with Seagate on HAMR vs ePMR technology (2026).

nodes.name: Pure Storage
nodes.sum: All-flash storage for AI training data pipelines; FlashBlade and DirectFlash for GPU-direct access. Q2 FY27 revenue $890M (+18%) with subscription ARR $1.7bn, 75%+ recurring (2026).

nodes.name: Delta Electronics
nodes.sum: Leading PSU and 800VDC busbar supplier for NVIDIA GB200/GB300 racks; DC power +55% y/y with data-centre power now ~30% of group revenue. Key supplier alongside Lite-On (2026).

nodes.name: Lite-On Technology
nodes.sum: Second-largest Taiwan server PSU maker after Delta; builds 54V/48V to 800VDC conversion modules for AI racks. Benefits from the Rubin transition that changes power-shelf specifications (2026).

nodes.name: nVent Electric
nodes.sum: Liquid cooling manifolds, rear-door heat exchangers and enclosures for data centres; Data Solutions segment +45% in Q2 2026. Acquired CoolTera (2024) for CDUs (2026).

nodes.name: CoolIT Systems (Ecolab)
nodes.sum: Direct-to-chip liquid cooling cold plates and rack-level CDUs deployed in NVIDIA DGX systems; estimated 15-20% of DLC cold plate market. Owned by Ecolab since 2024 (2026).

nodes.name: Boyd Corporation
nodes.sum: Private manufacturer of liquid cold plates, heat sinks and thermal interface materials for AI server OEMs; named among the four leading CDU/cold-plate suppliers alongside Vertiv, CoolIT and Schneider (2026).

nodes.name: Infineon Technologies
nodes.sum: Leading GaN and SiC power semiconductor maker for server VRMs and 800VDC busbars; AI server power content per rack rising from ~$200 to >$800. Q3 FY26 Power & Sensor +22% (2026).

nodes.name: Schneider Electric Motivair (liquid cooling)
nodes.sum: Schneider Electric's liquid cooling arm after the Motivair acquisition (2024); DLC CDUs and cold plates integrated into EcoStruxure. Named among the top-4 CDU vendors globally (2026).

nodes.name: Hitachi Energy
nodes.sum: One of four global transformer OEMs; opening a new US plant in South Carolina (2026) and expanding in Sweden. Transformer backlog growing >40% y/y; MV switchgear sold out through 2028.

nodes.name: ABB
nodes.sum: Global switchgear and power distribution maker; Electrification backlog ~$8bn at 1.2x book-to-bill. Q2 2026 Electrification +18%; new MV switchgear factory in the US for 2027 (2026).

nodes.name: Cummins
nodes.sum: Diesel and gas backup generator maker for data centres; Power Systems backlog >$5bn with lead times 40-60 weeks. Q2 2026 Power Systems +20% (2026).

nodes.name: Caterpillar
nodes.sum: Cat gensets (2-4 MW) are the default backup power for US data centres; Energy & Transportation orders +28% y/y with 30-50 week lead times. Q2 2026 segment +15% (2026).

nodes.name: Rolls-Royce
nodes.sum: MTU gas gensets and modular EnergyPacks for data centres; agreement with Equinix for 100+ MW on-site power. H1 2026 Power Systems orders +35% (2026).

nodes.name: Quanta Services
nodes.sum: Largest US electrical contractor; builds HV/MV substations and grid connections for data centres. Record total backlog $34bn; Q2 2026 Electric Power Infrastructure +22% (2026).

nodes.name: EMCOR Group
nodes.sum: Mechanical and electrical construction for data centres (~35% of revenue); backlog $12.5bn. Q2 2026 Electrical Construction +32%; skilled electrical labour is the binding constraint (2026).

nodes.name: Nexans
nodes.sum: Third-largest cable maker globally after Prysmian and NKT; adjusted backlog $7.5bn for HV/MV cables. Growing DC MV cable business with US plant expansion for DC-rated busbars (2026).

nodes.name: Hyundai Electric & Energy Systems
nodes.sum: Korean transformer maker opening a US plant (Alabama, 2027) alongside Hitachi Energy and Siemens Energy to address 128-week lead times, adding capacity to the global transformer oligopoly.

nodes.name: Hyosung Heavy Industries
nodes.sum: Korean heavy electrical maker producing power transformers, reactors and SF6-free switchgear; expanding US production to benefit from multi-year transformer lead-time dynamics (2026).

nodes.name: WEG
nodes.sum: Brazilian transformer, motor and generator maker; North America revenue +30% on DC and grid demand with a new US transformer plant in Houston. Q2 2026 GTD segment +22% (2026).

nodes.name: Southwire
nodes.sum: Largest US wire and cable manufacturer (private); supplies building wire, utility cable and DC power cable. Benefits from domestic manufacturing preference and rising copper demand for DC builds (2026).

nodes.name: Jacobs Solutions
nodes.sum: Engineering and programme management for hyperscale data centres; design-build for Microsoft and AWS campuses. Critical and digital infrastructure revenue ~$3bn/yr; Q3 FY26 CMS +20% (2026).

nodes.name: Turner Construction / Holder Construction (JV)
nodes.sum: Turner-Holder JV is among the largest DC general contractors in the US, building for Meta, Google and Microsoft. Skilled trade labour is the binding construction input (2026).

nodes.name: Powell Industries
nodes.sum: Custom-engineered MV switchgear and e-houses for data centres; record backlog $1.8bn at 1.3x book-to-bill. Q3 FY26 revenue +55% y/y; switchgear lead times 60-80 weeks (2026).

nodes.name: Medium-voltage switchgear

bn.rationale: Sold out through 2028; four-firm oligopoly; SF6 transition raising costs

nodes.sum: MV switchgear sold out through 2028; Eaton, ABB, Siemens Energy and Schneider are the big four. Lead times 40-80 weeks; SF6-free transition adds cost (2026).

nodes.name: UPS and battery energy storage for data centres
nodes.sum: Lithium-ion UPS replacing VRLA in new builds; 800VDC UPS needed for Rubin racks. Vertiv, Eaton and Schneider are the top three vendors; containerised BESS used as grid-side buffer (2026).

nodes.name: Constellation Energy
nodes.sum: Largest US nuclear fleet (32.4 GW total, ~21 GW nuclear); 20-year PPA with Microsoft to restart Three Mile Island 837 MW at ~$100/MWh; multi-year hyperscaler nuclear PPAs (2026).

nodes.name: Vistra Corp
nodes.sum: 41 GW diversified fleet including Comanche Peak nuclear (2.4 GW); agreed to supply Meta with up to 2 GW of nuclear power in a long-term PPA (2026).

nodes.name: Talen Energy
nodes.sum: 10.7 GW fleet anchored by Susquehanna Nuclear (2.5 GW); 960 MW behind-the-meter PPA with Amazon, approved by FERC with conditions; co-located capacity under development (Dec 2024).

nodes.name: NextEra Energy
nodes.sum: Largest US utility and global renewable generator: 73 GW total including ~35 GW renewables; FPL adding ~3 GW solar by 2028; exploring co-located solar+battery near data-centre loads (2026).

nodes.name: Dominion Energy
nodes.sum: Virginia utility serving Northern Virginia Data Center Alley (~70% of US colocation); interconnection queue 7+ years; monopoly grid provider to the largest data-centre cluster globally (2026).

nodes.name: Entergy Corporation
nodes.sum: Gulf-coast utility with ~30 GW of generation whose Louisiana and Mississippi territories are drawing hyperscale campuses; the 1.4 GW Grand Gulf nuclear station anchors clean-power PPAs, making Entergy a test of how fast regulated grids add AI load (2026).

nodes.name: Oklo
nodes.sum: Fast-fission SMR developer with more than 2 GW of signed data-centre power agreements but no operating reactor before the early 2030s; a relief path for the power layer only after 2030, so its $6bn market cap prices optionality, not capacity (2026).

nodes.name: US data-centre power additions (Goldman/EIA)
nodes.sum: US data-centre power additions: 8.5 GW (2025), 13.6 GW (2026), 36.3 GW (2027) per Goldman Sachs; gas and solar dominate new generation in EIA 860M monthly filings (Sep 2026).

nodes.name: Behind-the-meter gas generation for data centres
nodes.sum: Grid-queue bypass: OpenAI/Oracle 2.3 GW at Stargate, Meta on-site gas at Prometheus, Crusoe gas-powered campuses; avoids 3-7 year waits but raises emissions and permitting risk (2026).

nodes.name: Nuclear PPAs for data centres
nodes.sum: ~4-5 GW nuclear PPAs committed to hyperscalers by mid-2026: Microsoft-Constellation TMI (837 MW), Amazon-Talen Susquehanna (960 MW), Meta-Vistra Comanche Peak (up to 2 GW) (2026).

nodes.name: QTS Realty (Blackstone)
nodes.sum: Blackstone-acquired colocation: >2 GW gross power across 35+ data centres; Richmond campus 238 MW among largest US colocation facilities (Q2 2026).

nodes.name: Vantage Data Centers
nodes.sum: DigitalBridge-backed colocation: >2.5 GW across North America, EMEA and APAC; raised $18bn in debt financing 2025-26; Santa Clara, Ashburn and Montreal campuses (2026).

nodes.name: Aligned Data Centers
nodes.sum: Macquarie-backed colocation landlord with 500+ MW in operation and a 1.2 GW Phoenix campus under way for hyperscale tenants; one of the private GW-scale builders whose leases turn hyperscaler capex into energised halls (2026).

nodes.name: CyrusOne (KKR/GIP)
nodes.sum: KKR and GIP took CyrusOne private for $15bn in 2022; 50+ data centres in the US and Europe with ~1 GW under development make it a private-capital channel for hyperscale demand and a bellwether for infrastructure-fund appetite (2026).

nodes.name: Switch
nodes.sum: DigitalBridge-backed landlord whose Las Vegas SuperNAP campus scales to 1 GW and whose Reno Citadel campus adds more; a large private US colocation pipeline sold to hyperscalers and enterprises on renewable power contracts (2026).

nodes.name: Compass Datacenters
nodes.sum: Brookfield-backed colocation with the largest disclosed pipeline at >5 GW across North America; modular construction; major expansions in Dallas-Fort Worth and Northern Virginia (Q2 2026).

nodes.name: Galaxy Digital
nodes.sum: Crypto miner converting its Helios site in West Texas to AI hosting, with up to 800 MW committed to CoreWeave; the clearest example of energised bitcoin sites being re-priced as AI capacity, and a credit bet on its tenant (Sep 2026).

nodes.name: Nscale
nodes.sum: UK sovereign-cloud builder funded with $2bn+ from state-linked investors; its Narvik campus in Norway is under construction for Microsoft Azure, making it the Nordic route by which hyperscaler capacity lands on cheap hydro power (2026).

nodes.name: G42 / Khazna Data Centers
nodes.sum: Abu Dhabi sovereign AI: Khazna 300+ MW, Microsoft partnership for UAE sovereign AI, building 1 GW+ campus; Core42 cloud subsidiary provides regional compute (2026).

nodes.name: Humain (KSA)
nodes.sum: Saudi state AI company: $100bn+ infrastructure programme; planning two 500+ MW data centres in Riyadh and NEOM; partnered with AMD and NVIDIA for sovereign compute (2026).

nodes.name: Colossus 2 (Memphis)
nodes.sum: Largest operational single-campus by IT power at 946 MW in Memphis; B200/B300 GPUs serving Anthropic, Cursor and xAI; satellite-verified by Epoch AI (Sep 2026).

nodes.name: Anthropic-Amazon New Carlisle (Indiana)
nodes.sum: One of five 1 GW campuses in 2026; Amazon-owned Indiana campus with Anthropic as primary user; 910 MW satellite-derived estimate (Sep 2026).

nodes.name: Microsoft Fairwater Atlanta (Fayetteville, GA)
nodes.sum: One of five 1 GW-scale campuses in 2026; Microsoft Fairwater in Fayetteville GA at 636 MW; hosts OpenAI and Azure AI workloads (Sep 2026).

nodes.name: Meta Prometheus (New Albany, OH)
nodes.sum: One of five 1 GW-scale campuses in 2026; Meta in-house AI training in New Albany OH; 562 MW satellite-derived, reaching 1 GW (Sep 2026).

nodes.name: OpenAI Stargate Abilene (TX)
nodes.sum: One of five 1 GW-scale campuses in 2026; Oracle-owned Stargate in Abilene TX with OpenAI as primary tenant; 421 MW, ramping to 1.2 GW (Sep 2026).

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.sum: GPU cloud offering on-demand H100, B200 and B300 clusters to labs and startups; $800m Series D at a $4bn valuation in 2025 places it among the top-5 neoclouds, and its pricing is a public read on spot GPU rents (2026).

nodes.name: Crusoe Energy
nodes.sum: Builds behind-the-meter gas-powered AI data centres, including generation for Oracle's Abilene site; ~$3.4bn raised and a 1 GW+ target make it the main example of compute buyers bypassing the grid queue (Sep 2026).

nodes.name: Alibaba Cloud
nodes.sum: Largest cloud in China: Cloud Intelligence Group Q2 revenue $4.2bn (+26%); plans $52bn in AI infrastructure over three years; major inference supplier to DeepSeek and Chinese labs (Q2 2026).

nodes.name: Tencent Cloud
nodes.sum: Second-largest cloud in China; expanding AI compute with NVIDIA H20 and domestic accelerators; data-centre build-out in Guizhou and Qingyuan (2026).

nodes.name: ByteDance (Cloud/Volcengine)
nodes.sum: TikTok parent operating ~500,000 GPUs internally, among the largest GPU fleets globally; Volcengine cloud platform; one of the biggest NVIDIA H20 buyers in China (Sep 2026).

nodes.name: OpenAI Stargate Abilene (compute)
nodes.sum: Compute-side tenant view of Oracle-owned Stargate: OpenAI primary tenant at 421 MW ramping to 1.2 GW; NVIDIA $105bn credit support for 4.25 GW Ohio expansion (Sep 2026).

nodes.name: Anthropic-Amazon New Carlisle (compute)
nodes.sum: Compute-side tenant view of Amazon-owned New Carlisle: Anthropic as primary user at 910 MW; 1 GW Indiana facility (Sep 2026).

nodes.name: xAI Colossus 2 (compute)
nodes.sum: Compute-side view of Colossus 2 Memphis: >1M H100-equivalent GPUs at 946 MW, ramping to 2+ GW; largest single AI compute cluster in operation (Sep 2026).

nodes.name: Mistral AI
nodes.sum: Leading European frontier lab: Mistral Large 3 competitive with GPT-4o; Le Chat consumer product; raised ~$1.5bn at ~$7bn valuation with Microsoft and NVIDIA as investors (2026).

nodes.name: Alibaba Qwen (model family)
nodes.sum: China's leading open-weight model family: Qwen3-235B MoE takes 16.8% of OpenRouter tokens in Aug 2026; competitive on agent and coding benchmarks; integral to Alibaba Cloud.

nodes.name: Moonshot AI (Kimi)
nodes.sum: Beijing frontier lab with Kimi 2M-token-context product; raised $1bn+ from Alibaba and others; competing with DeepSeek in Chinese consumer and developer markets (2026).

nodes.name: Zhipu AI (GLM)
nodes.sum: Beijing enterprise AI lab: GLM-4 models backed by Tencent; B2B focus competing with DeepSeek and Qwen for the Chinese enterprise market (2026).

nodes.name: ByteDance Seed (model team)
nodes.sum: ByteDance internal AI lab training on ~500,000 GPUs; Doubao chatbot with 150M+ users; the largest compute user among Chinese labs (2026).

nodes.name: Safe Superintelligence Inc (SSI)
nodes.sum: Safety-focused frontier lab founded by Ilya Sutskever (ex-OpenAI chief scientist); raised $1bn at $5bn valuation; pure alignment research with no products yet (2026).

nodes.name: Cohere
nodes.sum: Enterprise-focused lab: Command R+ for RAG and on-premises deployment; raised $500m Series D at $5.5bn valuation; NVIDIA and Oracle investors (2026).

nodes.name: Microsoft AI (MAI models)
nodes.sum: Microsoft internal model arm: MAI-1 and Phi series with Phi-4-reasoning at frontier small-model performance; complements the OpenAI partnership for Azure services (2026).

nodes.name: Amazon Nova (models)
nodes.sum: Amazon internal model family: Nova Pro, Lite and Micro on Bedrock; trained on custom Trainium silicon; complements third-party models on AWS (Jul 2026).

nodes.name: SambaNova Systems
nodes.sum: Custom-silicon inference provider: RDU hardware with fastest open-weight benchmarks; SambaNova Cloud service; raised $1.1bn; competes on throughput (2026).

nodes.name: Hugging Face
nodes.sum: Largest open-source ML platform: >1M hosted models; Inference Endpoints and Spaces; hub for open-weight distribution; partnered with all three top clouds; valued at $4.5bn (2026).

nodes.name: Azure OpenAI Service
nodes.sum: Primary enterprise channel for GPT-4o and o-series: >60% of Fortune 500 using the service; majority of OpenAI enterprise revenue flows through Azure (Jul 2026).

nodes.name: Google Vertex AI
nodes.sum: Google Cloud managed ML platform: hosts Gemini, Claude and 200+ models via Model Garden; integral to Cloud's 82% revenue growth (Jul 2026).

nodes.name: Token price index
nodes.sum: Frontier-tier token prices +~100% since Jan 2026 while mid-tier fell 36%; effective prices fell 41% since March as buyers route to cheaper models; 6x provider spread (Aug 2026).

nodes.name: NVIDIA GPU debt backstop
nodes.sum: NVIDIA's GPU residual-value backstop (launched Jul 2026) and ~$50bn in frontier-lab investments; Firmus $25-30bn and SharonAI $4.88bn are first structures at 70-80% LTV.

nodes.name: Data-centre credit market
nodes.sum: Data-centre bond and loan issuance hit $334bn YTD Aug 2026 vs $185.5bn in all of 2025; ~80% of securities since early 2025 trade wider than issue. $1.4T funding gap.

nodes.name: Alphabet landlord backstops
nodes.sum: Alphabet landlord backstop deals: Cipher Barber Lake $1.73bn + warrants, TeraWulf $3.2bn + ~14% equity, Hut 8 fully backed. Vendor finance that moves credit risk upstream.

nodes.name: Situational Awareness LP
nodes.sum: AI-focused fund that rose +439% to Jun 2026 then fell 67% in Jul on ~4x leverage; sold ~$16bn public book to Citadel at ~10% discount.

nodes.name: AI credit tracker
nodes.sum: Market segment tracking AI credit conditions: hyperscaler debt share of capex rose from 9% (FY2024) to 32% (mid-2026); CoreWeave CDS implies ~50% cumulative default probability at 855bp.

nodes.name: US investment-grade bond market
nodes.sum: AI's growing share of US IG issuance: from 3.8% in 2024 to ~23.7% in H1 2026. DC securitisation hit $61bn YTD vs $4bn in 2020; first AAA DC ABS issued Jul 2026.

nodes.name: Hyperscaler long-term debt tracker
nodes.sum: Long-term debt at 30 Jun 2026, from the filings: Alphabet $98.2bn (+111% in six months), Amazon $128.9bn (+96%), Meta $83.7bn, CoreWeave $35.1bn, Oracle ~$130bn (cut to BBB-). Roughly $572bn across the six, about $54bn more than the previous estimate.

nodes.name: Neutral rate (r*) estimates
nodes.sum: Real neutral rate (r*) estimates: NY Fed HLW at 1.65% (Q2 2026, up from 1.36% in Q1 2025); Kim-Wright term premium 96bp on 11 Sep 2026, up from 48bp in mid-2025. The rates thesis is the current regime.

nodes.name: IG credit spread monitor
nodes.sum: IG spreads by rating, from FRED (17 Sep 2026): AAA 39bp, AA 57bp, A 66bp, BBB 95bp, 1-3y 47bp, 15+ year 98bp. The quality short end has widened modestly since end-2025 while BBB and the long end are flat to tighter -- hyperscaler duration supply shows up in term premium, not in corporate spreads.

nodes.name: AI-related CDS tracker
nodes.sum: AI-related CDS: CoreWeave 5y at 855bp (~50% implied default), Oracle tripled to 215bp, NVIDIA doubled to 82bp, Alphabet widened to 67bp. The real-time credit stress gauge.

nodes.name: Danish mortgage rates and variable-rate exposure
nodes.sum: Danish mortgage exposure: 72% of new loans variable-rate (Mar 2026); Nationalbanken hiked to 2.10% (Sep 2026). Danish households pay first for AI-driven global rate rises.

nodes.name: Data-centre securitisation market
nodes.sum: Data-centre securitisation: $61bn YTD Jul 2026 up from $4bn in 2020. ~80% of DC securities since early 2025 trade wider than issue; first AAA DC ABS issued Jul 2026.
